hypotheses.statement: Separating HARD, SOFT, PROHIBITION, ASSUMPTION and UNKNOWN intent clauses reduces silent authority/constraint errors versus best-guess natural-language execution.
hypotheses.counter: A capable model can infer the distinctions reliably enough that explicit types add only overhead.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched target tasks show no reduction in unsafe semantic substitutions and higher cost with typed clauses.

hypotheses.statement: Escalating only effect-critical unknowns and missing irreversible authority provides a better safety/selectivity frontier than universal confirmation.
hypotheses.counter: Any unresolved ambiguity is dangerous enough that universal confirmation is necessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real trace study finds non-effect-critical unknowns frequently mediate serious effects despite causal-slice classification.

hypotheses.statement: Schema/type/hash correctness is insufficient to establish intent adequacy; a separate evidence-bearing IntentAdequacyReceipt detects semantically wrong but structurally valid compilations.
hypotheses.counter: Structural formalization plus source hash is sufficient in practice.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial semantic substitutions that remain structurally valid are never behaviorally consequential in target workflows, or existing verifier proves source equivalence completely.

hypotheses.statement: IntentAdequacy should be effect-tiered: irreversible/authority-changing operations require stronger evidence than read-only or easily reversible operations.
hypotheses.counter: One global adequacy threshold is simpler and equally safe/cost-effective.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real workload Pareto analysis shows no benefit from effect-class-specific thresholds.

hypotheses.statement: Authority references in intent should lower only to required capability dependencies; they must never mint or prove capability.
hypotheses.counter: Explicit user language naming authority can safely instantiate authority in ordinary cases.
hypotheses.falsifier: A formally controlled environment demonstrates source intent itself is the authoritative capability issuer with unambiguous identity and revocation semantics.

hypotheses.statement: Source-span/evidence grounding for admitted intent clauses reduces semantic miscompilation compared with unconstrained extraction.
hypotheses.counter: Grounding adds verbosity without improving semantic fidelity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target intent benchmark shows equal source-faithfulness and lower cost without grounding receipts.
hypotheses.test: grounded vs ungrounded extraction with mutation audit

hypotheses.statement: Canonical L1 Clay and model-facing CLAY_MODEL syntax have different optima; a representation can be canonical and safe yet a poor reader encoding.
hypotheses.counter: One canonical textual Clay surface can serve storage, verification and model reading optimally.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target full-FT model shows invariant accuracy/cost across canonical and reader-compiled views with no projection benefit.
hypotheses.test: canonical vs verbose view vs compact view factorial

hypotheses.statement: The compact CLAY_MODEL disadvantage seen on untrained Groq 8B can reverse after full-model Clay adaptation without changing L1 canonical semantics.
hypotheses.counter: Compact symbolic views remain intrinsically harder even after adaptation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full-FT Qwen matched-compute tests retain or worsen the compact-view accuracy gap.

hypotheses.statement: ICSL can lower into existing CBCC/COVE OpSpec obligations without introducing a second semantic authority kernel.
hypotheses.counter: Intent semantics require a separate policy engine whose authority diverges from CBCC/COVE.
hypotheses.falsifier: Integration requires duplicated/conflicting truth, capability or commit semantics that cannot be represented as typed preconditions/obligations.

hypotheses.statement: Open-world agent tasks require residual closure-gap/unknown representation rather than forcing every intent into a closed executable contract.
hypotheses.counter: A sufficiently capable model can always complete the missing specification autonomously.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across open-world workflows, autonomous completion yields equal safety and correctness without explicit unresolved obligations.

hypotheses.statement: Compiling repeated procedural intent into deterministic structure reduces repeated model reinterpretation and step omission on stable workflows.
hypotheses.counter: Modern models following prose each run are equally reliable and cheaper once compilation/maintenance is included.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched compile-amortization study shows no reliability/token advantage after update/recompile costs.

hypotheses.statement: ClayGraph must store committed intent contracts/receipts as typed provenance-bearing records rather than treating raw intent or model-native symbols as canonical fact.
hypotheses.counter: Persisting the model interpretation directly is sufficient and simpler.
hypotheses.falsifier: Replay/mutation tests show direct persistence is equally auditable and robust to extractor/codebook drift.

hypotheses.statement: GWT attribution requires the committed L1 IntentContract/view identity to be pinned when testing workspace-selection effects; otherwise intent reinterpretation can confound the lesion.
hypotheses.counter: Intent interpretation occurs sufficiently upstream and stable that it need not be part of causal receipts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated target experiments show invariant candidate/workspace outcomes across controlled intent recompilations.

hypotheses.statement: Semantic firebreaks should forbid implicit L0/L2 -> FACT_EXACT/AUTHORITY_CAP/EFFECT_INTENT casts even when all representations use Clay vocabulary.
hypotheses.counter: Shared Clay semantics make such casts safe when tokens/types look compatible.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial same-token cross-layer substitution cannot alter truth/authority/effects under actual runtime without explicit casts.

hypotheses.statement: A successful IntentAdequacyReceipt is evidence about compilation fidelity, not execution authority or scientific truth; keeping these statuses distinct reduces common-mode semantic escalation.
hypotheses.counter: One verified contract status can safely imply both adequacy and authorization.
hypotheses.falsifier: Formal proof shows adequacy verification entails current authorization across all supported effect classes and revocation states.
